newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ZOLA GOAL GIVES ITALY VITAL WORLD CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZOLA GOAL GIVES ITALY VITAL WORLD CUP WIN.

text.p: Italy became the first team ever to beat England at home in a World Cup qualifier when a 19th-minute goal from Gianfranco Zola gave them a 1-0 victory at Wembley Stadium on Wednesday night.

Zola, who plays for London club Chelsea, slammed the ball past England goalkeeper Ian Walker after a long raking pass from Alessandro Costacurta eluded defenders Stuart Pearce and Sol Campbell, allowing Zola the space to control the ball and fire it home at the near post.

The result ended England's 100 percent start in their group two qualifying campaign, leaving them with nine points from four matches, but Italy have maintained their perfect start with their third straight win.

The match started brightly for England, who had played 28 home qualifiers since the early 1950s without defeat, but Italy gradually took control through Alessandro Costacurta and Demetrio Albertini who dictated much of their play.

England played with plenty of spirit and determination, going close to scoring through Matt Le Tissier, Graeme Le Saux and Paul Ince in the closing stages, but they could do nothing in the end to break down a superbly marshalled Italian defence.
